speech:
Alright, Grizzly Rips, pull up a chair. Today's a B-minus, and that's an honest B-minus. 5 wins, 1 draw, 3 losses, 27 scored, 19 let in. That's better than our usual, but it came with a bruise we can't ignore.

We woke up in Division 3 with 5 of 12 points and 1 chance left. We spent it losing 1-2 to Flex musix, then dropped the relegation match 2-3 to NorthStar. That's relegated, plain and simple. Then y'all dusted yourselves off, climbed straight into a promotion series, and now sit at 1 and 1. One more win and we're back where we started. The first half of the day earned 4 points; the second half earned 12. That tells me the fight was there. It just showed up late to the dance.

And we're still leaking. 2.11 conceded per match won't hold up in Division 3.

buddskees, you were the engine. An 8.54 against your usual 7.8, 8 assists, and a perfect 10.0 against Drew Peacox, your second one for us. Your tackling jumped to 78% from a usual 53%. That's somebody who came to work. But you rage quit match 7. You were winning 6-2 with a 10.0 on the board, and you still walked out. I can't make sense of that, and the team can't afford it. Match 3 against Flex musix you put 0% of your shots on target, and Stinging Beez's best midfielder outplayed you 9.8 to 7.2 in the match we needed.

PhogsToffees, 11 goals and 8 assists. You were the most dangerous person on the pitch, and in the Drew Peacox 5-3 everything you shot went in. But match 3 was rough: a 6.6, 12 missed tackles, and 21 giveaways. That loss is the one that sent us down. Your tackling sat at 16% all day, 9 won from 56 tries. I love that you're chasing. Now chase smarter.

BellyTb1, solid day, a 7.89 above your 7.71, and 8 goals. In match 4 you stepped up with 7 tackle attempts when it mattered. But in match 6 you went 0 for 5 in tackles with 11 giveaways, and against NorthStar in the promotion opener you dipped to a 6.4.

Now, finishing. BellyTb1 put 26 of 34 on target, and PhogsToffees put 21 of 33. That's great aim at the wrong spot. Keepers love a shot right down the middle. Aim for the corners. From an angle, finesse it to the far post. One-on-one, go low and hard across the keeper, because that's the toughest save and the easiest rebound. Use timed finishing only when you trust it.

Here's the thing, friends. A tree that gets knocked down a hill grows roots wherever it lands, and today y'all grew roots fast. We've got one match standing between us and getting back home. I believe in this group like I believe a biscuit needs gravy. Rest up, and let's go win it together.
